name: Dobharchú
text: Dobharchú, anglicised Dorraghow, is the Irish word for the otter. MacKillop treats him as the father of all otters and the king called Iring of the lakes. His snout has the strength to break through a rock. The Dobharchú is a figure of fear on land. He can kill people and animals. He can drink their blood. The lore of the great otter belongs to the wider Irish folk tradition about water-animals with human-like power.
